payload: I was the one who placed the April satay order for Merrivale. Two days later, facilities found an EpiPen cap in the boardroom trash — someone in that room used it and said nothing. No one reported an allergy afterward, no one filed anything, and the dietary register still shows nothing for that party. The absence of a recorded allergy is not clearance; it is a gap I created and cannot close. Fernhill's menu says they cannot certify any tray peanut-free, and the satay sauce is not optional. The register is only as good as what people pass on, and what people pass on after a quiet anaphylaxis scare is apparently nothing. So this is not a one-off caution. It is a permanent reflex: no peanut-containing item goes to the office on my order, for any meeting, whoever asks — not until every person in the room has confirmed their status in writing to me. The Harvest Grain Tray is the standing substitute. If someone wants to override that, they can place the order themselves under their own name. This is not about preference. I put peanuts in front of someone whose airway closed, and I am not doing it again.
